mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating economic activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, particularly when accompanied by rising industrial production (INDPRO).
failure_condition: If GDPC1 and INDPRO both rise but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or if the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns drops below 0.3 in rolling 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing output, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially when accompanied by falling housing starts (HOUST).
failure_condition: If INDPRO and HOUST both decline but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if the negative correlation between manufacturing weakness and SPX returns exceeds -0.4 in rolling 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% signals restrictive monetary policy, which historically compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, particularly when unemployment (UNRATE) is below 5%.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 5.5% but UNRATE is above 5% and S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, or if the negative correlation between rate hikes and SPX returns weakens below -0.35 in rolling 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially when combined with declining payroll employment (PAYEMS).
failure_condition: If UNRATE and PAYEMS both decline but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if the negative correlation between labor weakness and SPX returns drops below -0.4 in rolling 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating household demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, particularly when accompanied by rising GDP growth (GDPC1).
failure_condition: If RSAFS and GDPC1 both rise but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances, or if the correlation between consumption growth and SPX returns weakens below 0.4 in rolling 3-year windows.
